I have resolved the issue by converting non-ASCII domain names to Punycode:

- Added [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/utils/encoding.py#L251-L253) in [django/utils/encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/utils/encoding.py) and used it across domain-encoding call sites in [django/core/mail/utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/core/mail/utils.py), [django/core/mail/message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/core/mail/message.py), [django/core/validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/core/validators.py), and [django/utils/html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/utils/html.py).
- Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16-L19) and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-e8d9zn_1/django/core/mail/message.py#L255-L262) so non-ASCII hostnames/domains used in `Message-ID` headers and SMTP connections are converted to Punycode.
